#### e-newsletter

## APRIL '25
---
|
* **From homeless to housed, Daly City mother shares family’s odyssey**
* **Dispatchers honored for answering the call**
* **County takes stand against bullying**
* **500 County Center wins another sustainability award**
* **Students learn about loneliness and connection during read-a-thon**
* **MTC grants county $8.6M for infrastructure projects**

---
| | |
---
|
# “This is an amazing family who put their children first in the most trying of times. Imagine having to choose between staying in a hotel or purchasing food while keeping your kids in school and parking discreetly near free WiFi spots so they could do their homework”
# **\- President David Canepa**
---
| | | | **2025 April e-newsletter** **500 County Center wins another sustainability award**

Dear friends,
I am proud to announce, as the San Mateo County President, that our County Office Building 3 in Redwood City has won the 2025 Green Building Award!

Cosponsored by Sustainable San Mateo County and the American Institute of Architects San Mateo County Chapter, 500 County Center is the first civic building in the United States to combine mass timber construction with a net-zero-energy design, achieving an 85% reduction in structural embodied carbon.

The 5-story building also wont the “Best of the Best” Award for Sustainability from Engineering News-Record this year.

With features such as solar panels, automated systems, biotreatment areas, and a focus on employee well-being, this project sets a new benchmark for sustainable public buildings. Here’s to a healthier, more sustainable future!

Save the date for the official ribbon cutting of 500 County Center as San Mateo County partners with the San Mateo County History Museum to celebrate the 169th birthday of the County of San Mateo on May 15th at 5 p.m. in downtown Redwood City. Stay tuned for more details. **MTC grants county $8.6M for infrastructure projects**

Electric vehicle charging will ramp up significantly in San Mateo County and a new transformational regional mobility hub is coming to Daly City BART as the Metropolitan Transportation Commission approved $8.6 million in funding for transportation infrastructure projects throughout the county.

Grants for 5 EV charging infrastructure, electric bikeshare deployment and fleet electrification were approved for the cities of East Palo Alto, San Carlos, Portola Valley, Half Moon Bay and Menlo Park.

Colma and South San Francisco were also awarded grants for the design and technical assistance for two segments of the El Camino Real and Bicycle and Pedestrian Project.

And the biggest grant was awarded for the $3.8 million Daly City BART Mobility Hub that will transform the station into a community anchor that will enable travelers of all backgrounds and abilities to access multiple transportation options.

These options include shared scooters, bicycles, cars and public transit as well as wayfinding, improved lighting and other amenities that will enliven this incredibly important transit corridor linking San Mateo and San Francisco counties. **Students learn about loneliness and connection during read-a-thon**

Last month, I had the pleasure of hosting a read-along at Susan B. Anthony Elementary School in Daly City for a fifth-grade class as part of the weeklong read-a-thon!

I read “The Invisible String” by Patrice Karst, a beautiful story about loneliness and connection. It’s so important to talk about mental health with young students and remind them of the power of community. I am grateful for this experience!

The book was first published by in 2000. The inside flap of the dust jacket reads:

“Specifically written to calm a child’s fear of being apart from the ones they love, ‘The Invisible String’ ... delivers a compelling message in today’s uncertain times. Grownups and children everywhere who are looking for reassurance and reaffirmation of the transcendent power of love to bind, connect, and comfort will discover how easily they can ‘tug’ on each other’s heart with The Invisible String!”

I was thankful for the experience and grateful for the children’s response after reading this very uplifting book. **Dispatchers honored for answering the call**

I am proud to sponsor a proclamation declaring April 13-19 as Public Safety Dispatcher Week in honor of the incredible men and women who serve as the first point of contact in emergencies.

When someone dials 911, they’re often facing one of the worst moments of their life — a fire, medical emergency, crime in progress, or unfolding crisis. Before first responders arrive, it’s our dispatchers who answer the call, providing critical guidance, calming panicked voices, and ensuring help gets where it’s needed most.

In San Mateo County, our dispatchers handle hundreds of calls daily, making split-second, life-or-death decisions while staying composed under immense pressure. In 2024 alone 496,383 calls were answered; 364,459 incidents were handled; the busiest day had 2,559 calls; 30 languages were spoken; and 8,000 training hours were completed.

A special congratulations to Shanel Campana, Fire Specialist/Controller, for being named 2024 Dispatcher of the Year! Your dedication and excellence set the standard for public safety in our county.

And thanks to Director at County of San Mateo Office of Public Safety Communications Natasha Claire-Espino for her outstanding service and commitment to keeping our community safe. Your hard work does not go unnoticed!

To all our dispatchers: We see you, we appreciate you, and we thank you. Your resilience and commitment keep our community safe every single day.

**From homeless to housed, Daly City mother shares family’s odyssey**

Imagine having to choose between staying in a hotel or buying food for your children. For over a year, Daly City native Angelica Rodriguez and her children’s father lived in their van, doing everything they could to keep their boys safe, in school, and fed.

They parked near free Wi-Fi so homework could get done, used ice to keep Angelica’s insulin cold, and made every sacrifice to hold their family together.

Today, thanks to Angelica’s determination and the unwavering support of San Mateo County’s incredible staff and nonprofit partners, she and her children finally have a place to call home. Our County Housing Authority, Daly City Health Center, YMCA, LifeMoves, and Abode Services worked tirelessly to ensure this family found the stability they deserve.

The dedication of our county employees and nonprofit teams makes a life-changing difference every day, and I couldn’t be prouder of their commitment to lifting up our most vulnerable residents.

Their two-bedroom apartment, made possible through a federal voucher program, offers stability after years of uncertainty. This is more than just a story about housing—it’s about resilience, love, and a community that stepped up when it mattered most.

Let’s continue working together to ensure that no family in San Mateo County has to endure this journey alone.

Thank you to the San Mateo County Communications and Public Information team for highlighting this family’s uplifting story!

**County takes stand against bullying**

No one should ever feel unsafe, unheard, or unwelcome in their own community, especially our youth. Bullying can leave lasting scars, and it’s on all of us to create a culture of kindness, respect and inclusion.
On the Board of Supervisors, we have a duty not only to uphold the well-being of all residents of San Mateo County but also to create a community where every individual, particularly our youth, can thrive.

Last month the Board passed a resolution I sponsored that reaffirms the County’s unwavering commitment to standing up against youth bullying in all its forms and to promote a safe, respectful community where every young person can flourish.

The resolution calls on every department and every employee to actively engage in efforts to prevent bullying, to provide education, and to intervene when necessary.

This resolution also calls on us to listen to the voices of those who have been affected — our youth, families, and community members. By evaluating and improving our youth bullying prevention efforts regularly, we can ensure that we are always responsive to the evolving needs of our community.
**Interns wanted to join our team ** We are looking to add to our great group of interns we are currently working with. If you or someone you know may be interested in applying to my Internship Program, submitting this form is the first step: [https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=7388a4a4b3&e=c0babbc643 "https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9?fbclid=IwAR3YFH0mH828rtAUru5EFOO9GsMCasQYe1N7AUrmwAwBf30JTtXOSeCzKjs"). You can also reach out to Mike Richardson on my staff directly with any questions at [mrichardson@smcgov.org](mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org "mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org"). In friendship,
**DAVID J. CANEPA**
President, San Mateo County Board of Supervisors

The SAVE Act would force every voter to prove their identity with a passport or birth certificate every time they register or update their registration. That doesn’t just effectively end online and mail-in voter registration — if passed, it’d have devastating effects on who gets access to the ballot box.
Studies show that millions of Americans can’t meet the SAVE Act’s paperwork requirements to register to vote, disproportionately affecting military voters, rural voters, tribal citizens, survivors of natural disasters, people of color, and working-class Americans.
**Let’s be clear about what this is about: making it more difficult for certain citizens to vote, all while claiming to address very-false claims of widespread voter fraud.**

clean_body: We need all hands on deck to stop this legislation from becoming law. | BREAKING: The SAVE Act just passed the House of Representatives. This is an extreme, anti-voter bill that could disenfranchise millions of eligible voters — and we must hold the line against it. = | = Peter — Imagine if you couldn't exercise your right to vote just because you don't have your original birth certificate or because you decided to change your last name when you got married. If extremists in Congress get their wish and pass the SAVE Act, that could be the reality for tens of millions of Americans. The SAVE Act is one of the biggest threats to voting rights we’ve seen in a generation — and we must do everything we can to prevent it from becoming law. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = The SAVE Act would force every voter to prove their identity with a passport or birth certificate every time they register or update their registration. That doesn’t just effectively end online and mail-in voter registration — if passed, it’d have devastating effects on who gets access to the ballot box. Studies show that millions of Americans can’t meet the SAVE Act’s paperwork requirements to register to vote, disproportionately affecting military voters, rural voters, tribal citizens, survivors of natural disasters, people of color, and working-class Americans. Let’s be clear about what this is about: making it more difficult for certain citizens to vote, all while claiming to address very-false claims of widespread voter fraud. = We’ll keep you posted on the latest. As someone who admires Senator Rand Paul for his principled stance in the U.S. Senate, I've come to value his commitment to individual liberty and free markets. His consistent advocacy for limited government connects with me, and I often find myself in agreement with his positions. At the same time, I've been a staunch supporter of President Donald Trump, a true outsider who I believe genuinely cares about restoring America's strength. Many of us see him as a necessary disruptor, perhaps our last hope to fix the economic and political mess left by decades of misguided policies. Yet, despite my support for both men, I find myself troubled by Trump's aggressive tariff policies--and Paul's opposition to them has given me pause.
My generation, now nearing retirement, feels caught in a vise. We've worked tirelessly, saved diligently, and pinned our hopes on a strong stock market to secure our future. The shift from company pensions to 401(k) plans forced us to rely on market performance, but Trump's tariffs are shaking that foundation. Tariffs, by raising the cost of imported goods like electronics, clothing, and even car parts, drive up prices and spark market volatility. When trade tensions flare, as they have in 2025, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq often tumble, eroding the savings we've spent decades building. A single market dip can wipe out thousands from a retirement account, leaving us with losses we may not have time to recover. It feels like we're paying the price for policies we didn't create, stuck cleaning up after the excesses of past generations while our children struggle to find their footing.
Senator Paul's opposition to Trump's tariffs aligns with my growing unease. Rooted in his libertarian belief in free markets, Paul argues that tariffs are taxes that hit American consumers and businesses hardest. Higher costs for imports don't just burden foreign governments--they raise the price of groceries, appliances, and gas for families like mine. Paul points to Kentucky's bourbon distillers and farmers, who've suffered from retaliatory tariffs abroad, as proof that trade wars hurt local economies. He dismisses the idea that trade deficits justify tariffs, insisting that voluntary trade fuels prosperity, not harm. His warnings about economic fallout ring true when I see my grocery bill climb or my retirement portfolio shrink.
Paul also raises a deeper concern: Trump's use of emergency powers to impose tariffs sidesteps Congress, undermining the Constitution's checks and balances. His push for the No Taxation Without Representation Act of 2025 reflects a principled stand against executive overreach--a reminder of why I respect him. Historically, Paul notes, tariffs like the 1890 McKinley Tariff or the 1930 Smoot-Hawley Tariff triggered economic pain and political losses for Republicans. He fears a repeat could jeopardize the GOP's future, a worry I share as someone who wants conservative values to endure.
While I believe in Trump's vision, Paul's arguments make me question whether tariffs are worth the cost. They may protect some industries, but for those nearing retirement like me, facing higher prices and a shaky market, the burden feels heavy. Paul's principled resistance offers a sobering perspective--one that balances my hope for America's revival with the reality of who pays the price.

Paul also raises a deeper concern: Trump's use of emergency powers to impose tariffs sidesteps Congress, undermining the Constitution's checks and balances. His push for the No Taxation Without Representation Act of 2025 reflects a principled stand against executive overreach--a reminder of why I respect him. Historically, Paul notes, tariffs like the 1890 McKinley Tariff or the 1930 Smoot-Hawley Tariff triggered economic pain and political losses for Republicans. He fears a repeat could jeopardize the GOP's future, a worry I share as someone who wants conservative values to endure. While I believe in Trump's vision, Paul's arguments make me question whether tariffs are worth the cost. They may protect some industries, but for those nearing retirement like me, facing higher prices and a shaky market, the burden feels heavy. Paul's principled resistance offers a sobering perspective--one that balances my hope for America's revival with the reality of who pays the price. In 2020, Metro began pushing forward initiatives to address homelessness and move thousands of people off the streets in the Region. | | | [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.nTQp_FEIcSHl649vCJCicgFl4-m14JFRBrcYNYwfP9JIvmBnHU0VGpOT6rptE2SR6E78Ff5HQrMYZCajUoqbkOsfAEZQMwkF7Ez2d79gy1HYnpV-6Zb6QTwzR5_nufz1lEOGPwCsz7hol-hXoa7chArO88IHx1y9OQ74FWWDhnXOgkwDEttCzLYZk-AcMP7bjpxJS2_047nJyaVXgOqdClfuSZIT8ytT0BWIQQ-VB2CQTeFu0P1XYFyNxDneOgTi7_Wd61oVzTMaZvjc_tG8qg/4fk/6PLa0JlfTzKmcU6eXi6vOA/h0/h001.zN6fTg6zOPXufu_eY6FvHAEnb_1scZZqKckF_3AU7N0) Peter**,** **Homelessness and the lack of affordable housing are our region's most urgent problems.** Its causes are complex and long-standing, and solutions need to be flexible, accountable, and forward-thinking. **In 2020, Metro began putting forth initiatives to address homelessness and move thousands of people off the streets in the region.** While our work has been a step in the right direction, there is more work that needs to be done to address homelessness fully.
### [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtU7IN3usUMtZznyYbhtcGJuLYNnr-KuWgOb5JbgtD1jRNuWTVXBBiC9yZB67KfK9Cf_gHZzULNVcUUCQqoJp3RRWZbHaa9evTAllbPl4Uj-sNWFu4vAStw4agFWTF_TZCaY6A9RPbNNv9cwulqrVa6hJbbvFSwAQooGTi0DRcwKMzi7wppCE0yMoL5eLb8KKYj7XsKJTWqhsJKzRIP1mcrPHNXcAECwzkn8XQ0Fn85UMxIqL4d4sCq1xotxXD8AA3oHSg5BZQy067EKWnbq9n3Epb55cNbFMOS2By-LgxrGEd6C77m0ns5eH3y96-MAqZM3aPbzQBpf-sNXjdU6hMZE1od0t5_21ZFt8reZoVPi4/4fk/6PLa0JlfTzKmcU6eXi6vOA/h1/h001.RyyRG6nngpB6Cjny2JaCOfqtc6H1tUkBp4Y-qeC6pds)

**Voters are expecting results, and Metro is ready to deliver. Over the past 5 years, the Supportive Housing Services program has had both successes and challenges. We've learned how important this work is - and what we must do to make it better. That's why Metro is proposing important changes to lead the efforts on addressing homelessness in the region:****

**
* Streamline oversight with a single committee that sets clear regional goals, with more accountability and efficiency.
* Adjusting who pays the regional homeless service tax while reducing the tax rate.
* And because this work must continue if we are going to be seriously move the needle, extending the tax for another 20 years to ensure the infrastructure we are creating does not fall by the wayside.

We can't continue business as usual, but making the change we need will take building trust, hope, and confidence among all of our neighbors. Part of the work of Neighbors Across the Region is to create new direct lines of communication (like this one) with the people we serve. The work that we want to push forward this spring will not be possible without you. We need your help to ensure these reforms get adopted and to put our best foot forward in moving this region in a better direction for everyone. **Big decisions need to be made to help our region name: New PA Project Education Fund
subject: Liberation is not only history, it’s a call to action
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the New PA Project Education Fund
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/NPP_Ed_logo_RGB_green1-01.jpg]
Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Yesterday, the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) bill passed the U.S. House 220 to 208 [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-passes-bill-requiring-proof-citizenship-vote-federal-elections-rcna200586] , and is now headed to the Senate.
This bill, if it passes the Senate, would require prospective voters to show proof of U.S. citizenship in order to register to vote, a move that will create unnecessary barriers for over 21 million of eligible U.S. citizens [https://www.politicspa.com/what-is-the-save-act-and-why-did-the-house-pass-it/141191/] .
Actions like these disproportionately harm working people, young voters, new Americans, anyone who has changed their name, such as married people taking their spouse's last name, and Black and brown communities.
As a voting rights organization, we are vehemently opposed to any additional barriers that would make it more difficult to register to vote, and also make it more difficult for our voices to be heard at the ballot box.
REGISTER TO VOTE [https://vote.pa/check/?org=nppef]
How do bills become law?
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Screenshot%202025-04-11%20105706.png]
A bill is a proposal for a new law or a change to an existing law. The idea for a bill can come from anyone. It could be a member of the U.S. Senate or House of Representatives, or even by people or citizen groups who recommend a new or amended law to a member of Congress that represents them.
Once a bill is introduced, or presented in either body, it is assigned to a committee whose members will research, discuss, and make any necessary changes to the bill.
The bill is then put before that chamber (U.S. House or Senate) to be voted on.
If the bill passes in one body of Congress, it goes to the other body to go through a similar process of research, discussion, changes, and voting (If it started in the House then it goes to the Senate and vice versa).
Once both bodies have passed the bill, they need to review if there were any changes, to make sure they pass the same version. If it passes, it goes to the president.
The president then either approves the bill and signs it into law, making it an act . Or the president rejects the bill. This is called a veto .
If the president chooses to veto a bill, in most cases Congress can vote to override that veto and the bill becomes a law . But if the president does not sign off on a bill and it remains unsigned when Congress is no longer in session, the bill will be vetoed by default. This action is called a pocket veto, and it cannot be overridden by Congress .
The SAVE act is not really an act. It is a bill that has passed the House. In order to become an act, the Senate would have to pass it, and then the president would have to sign it, and maybe adjust the name or it would become the "SAVE act Act" if it became law.
On this week, 159 years ago
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Screenshot%202025-04-10%20185920.png] This week, 159 years ago the Civil Rights Act of 1866 was passed.
It declared that anyone born in the United States was a citizen, regardless of their race or previous condition of slavery.
This law was passed about one year after the abolition of slavery to counteract discriminatory "Black Codes" passed by many southern states after the Civil War. The Codes limited the freedoms of Black people.
President Andrew Johnson initially vetoed the bill, but Congress overrode the veto, and the Act became law on April 9, 1866.
Today, 159 years later, there are some people who are trying to dismantle these rights - by, for example, proposing the end of birthright citizenship.

# The cruelty is their point.
---

name: Jim Schultz
subject: Keith Ellison Caught Lying About $250M Feeding Our Future Fraud
body:
Explosive new audio proves Keith Ellison lied, took campaign cash from fraudsters who stole $250M meant to feed low-income kids during the pandemic.

| | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us18.campaign-archive.com/?e=baf210d431&u=e307c9beec837f7456d65a5e6&id=07e092929a)
---
| | | |
---
| Friend,
Newly released [audio recordings](https://growthmn.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e307c9beec837f7456d65a5e6&id=40f6ffcef1&e=baf210d431) obtained by the _Center of the American Experiment_ have exposed the truth: Attorney General Keith Ellison misled the public about his role in the largest fraud in Minnesota history—then took campaign contributions from the very people behind it.
In my [latest op-ed for _Alpha News_](https://growthmn.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e307c9beec837f7456d65a5e6&id=10b4dd6139&e=baf210d431) , I lay out what’s on the recording—and what it means for anyone who cares about the rule of law, taxpayer accountability, and basic integrity in public office.
Here’s what you need to know:
In December 2021, Ellison held a closed-door meeting inside his official government office with individuals later indicted in the [$250 million Feeding Our Future scandal](https://growthmn.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e307c9beec837f7456d65a5e6&id=1171f52984&e=baf210d431). On the tape, Ellison admits he had never heard of the fraud—despite later claiming publicly that his office had been working the case _“for two solid years.”_
That was a lie.
Just nine days after the meeting, Ellison accepted [$10,000 in campaign contributions](https://growthmn.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e307c9beec837f7456d65a5e6&id=669f38b1ab&e=baf210d431) from attendees tied to the fraud. Instead of investigating, he dismissed oversight concerns as _“piddly, stupid stuff,”_ sympathized with the fraudsters, and pledged to _“fight”_ the very state agencies trying to expose them.

subject: The offices we hold demand a higher standard of ethics

body:
If you are in a position of public trust, you shouldn’t be trading stocks. None of us should use our positions for financial gain. Period.
#

Friend —
When you’re elected to federal office, you get access to a lot of sensitive information. A lot of that information could be used for financial gain. And, if you ask me, that’s a conflict of interest.
We can all agree that members of Congress shouldn’t be allowed to trade stocks. That’s why I put all of my assets in a blind trust when I became a United States Senator.
Now, this Tuesday, Trump told all of his followers on X that it was a great time to buy. A few hours later, he announced that the tariffs he put in place were all getting scaled back to 10% — with the exception of the ones still applied to China. Those tariffs tanked the economy, and when he announced they were off, the markets temporarily spiked.
It certainly looks like President Trump, Elon Musk, his Administration, his family, his friends, and his closest supporters in Congress positioned themselves to benefit from that. If that’s the case, the corruption is absolutely staggering. I’m pushing to get to the bottom of it.
The leaders of our country must be held to a higher standard than this, and something has to change.
So, today, I’m renewing my call for Congress to meet my standard — and I am expanding it to the entire Trump Administration. If you are in a position of public trust, you shouldn’t be trading stocks. None of us should use our positions for financial gain. Period.
**If you’d like to join me, please:[Add your name and tell Congress and the Trump Administration to stop trading stocks and put their assets in a blind trust. We must meet the ethical standard that our offices demand. Anything less is unacceptable. **](https://act.markkelly.com/signup/stocks_em_april25/?source=em250411-1-500&akid=6040%2E6688874%2EDw4D6d)

Mark

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 4/11/2025
body:
Polis signs SB25-003 into law after months of protest and 95,000 petitions
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/ses41b1a081)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s3r2e609a3d)**
| | Hi everyone,
Listen to today's **Mountain Minute Podcast** [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s8q530e7dcb), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s5o6ba59a67) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s9p50c8274a)! Here is a summary of today's top stories: ****
**🏛️ Colorado Legislative Session Updates...** Governor Polis [quietly signed](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s8l43a1c682) SB25-003, a sweeping semi-auto gun ban, despite 95,000 petitions urging a veto. HB25-1169 is drawing fire for [overriding local zoning](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s1l7d952127) on church and school properties, and lawmakers [advanced a $44B budget](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s7uc632c3ad) amid a $1.2B deficit and rising GOP opposition. Meanwhile, faith leaders are urging Polis to veto a new bill that would force taxpayers to [fund abortions through Medicaid](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s7pa9244e15), calling it a moral and constitutional betrayal.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** The Cherry Creek Republican Women met this week to discuss everything from [school book controversies](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s2l9a35aa1f) to Centennial’s leadership in infrastructure and the launch of a new women’s pro soccer team.

🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Consumer prices dropped in March—defying predictions of “tarifflation” and delivering [a win for Trump’s economic agenda](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s4g9c5158dd). The CPI fell 0.1%, with energy and goods leading the decline, backing Trump’s promise to fight inflation through bold trade policy.

🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** Garbo sounds the alarm on HB25-1312, warning it opens the door for the state to seize children from parents over pronoun disagreements—a fundamental [assault on parental rights and liberty](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s1p559381be).

This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, April 11, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Polis signs SB25-003 into law after months of protest and 95,000 petitions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s8idbaadf4a)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s6i56ee2c13)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s7j4de3bc91)
In the end, Governor Jared Polis didn’t make a speech. He didn’t stand before cameras or take questions. He didn’t even put the signing on his public calendar.
On April 9, behind closed doors and without public ceremony, Polis signed Senate Bill 25-003 into law—legislation that critics say is one of the most restrictive gun ownership laws in the country. The signing came after months of resistance from Colorado citizens, lawmakers and small business owners who warned the bill was not only unconstitutional, but economically and socially devastating.
Here’s how it happened.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s2k502d742c)**
|
---
The Rocky Mountain Voice is a 501(c)(3) that exists to promote informed civic engagement and the principles of self-governance through enterprise reporting on public policy, politics, government, and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s3n8cd65d7e)
|
---
**[HB25-1169 would strip local control, override zoning to force housing on church and school property](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s5q0d332b4d)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s6g77a899c6)
* HB25-1169 would override local zoning laws to mandate housing development on land owned by churches and schools—regardless of density, parking, or public input—without requiring affordability.
* Local leaders like Mayor Stephanie Piko argue the bill does nothing to address real housing barriers like cost and liability, and instead undermines local control while favoring select landowners.
* Douglas County is pursuing home rule to push back against state overreach, with growing concern the bill will lead to high-density housing in residential neighborhoods without consent.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s2p2514ed48)**
|
---
**[Garbo: With HB25-1312, the state can claim your kids and call it compassion](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s5t5637694c)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s4kbf0fb257)
* HB25-1312 redefines child abuse to include “misgendering” or “deadnaming,” allowing the state to strip custody from parents who don’t affirm a child’s self-declared gender identity.
* Garbo warns the bill replaces parental authority with government ideology, criminalizing dissent and threatening families who reject gender orthodoxy.
* He argues the bill ignores scientific debate and lived experience from detransitioners, calling it a dangerous precedent that sacrifices children’s well-being for political conformity.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s2v0600e786)**
|
---
**[Books, ballgames and bold leadership: Cherry Creek Republican Women tackle hot topics](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/seu0cf40e1b)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s2g18db5de3)
* At a Cherry Creek Republican Women luncheon, Elizabeth Superintendent Dan Snowberger defended the district’s decision to remove explicit books from school libraries, citing community standards; the federal court has paused an order to return them pending further review.
* Centennial Mayor Stephanie Piko shared updates on public safety, smart infrastructure, and a new 12,000-seat stadium for a women’s pro soccer team launching in 2026—already drawing over 10,000 season ticket deposits.
* Piko also pushed back [against HB25-1169](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s3je1d09ab4), warning it would worsen housing challenges by overriding local zoning authority and creating more red tape for already-approved projects.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s6k9c9897c9)**
|
---
** ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[“Celebrate the win”: Boebert’s gray wolf delisting bill clears key House committee](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s8la9bdf62d)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s5n0f390fed)****BY JEN SCHUMANN****| STATE | APRIL 9** _In rural Colorado, the fight over wolves isn’t just about wildlife—it’s about life and livelihoods. On Tuesday, a bill sponsored by Reps. Lauren Boebert and Tom Tiffany passed a key House committee, aiming to take gray wolves off the Endangered Species List and block federal courts from reversing the move._
__
**[New council, new direction: Grand Junction voters back reform candidates](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s4pf00f0c35)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/sbv922b559d)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | APRIL 9** _All four City Council seats up for election in Grand Junction this April have been claimed by candidates promising a new direction for the city. While official results won’t be certified until later this month, the margins are clear—and the message from voters, even clearer._
__
**[The fine print of SB25-063: Speak up about inappropriate books in schools, get doxxed](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s5qcc54e44e)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._lnDQ/s5pbc0d35b7)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | APRIL 8** _When Colorado lawmakers debated Senate Bill 25-063—titled the “Freedom to Read Act”—most eyes focused on the usual battle lines: controversial books, age appropriateness and the role of librarians. But tucked inside the bill is something less publicized—and more dangerous to parents who dare to speak up._
__

It’s been a hell of a week, folks.
In case you missed it, Trump imposed tariffs on pretty much every country in the world — even places with _no human population_.
With these tariffs in place, everything, from coffee to gaming consoles, will be more expensive. **Billionaires and massive corporations will be just fine, but for those of us who can barely afford to buy eggs, these tariffs are going to hurt.**
Even with a 90-day pause in place for most countries’ tariffs, the looming threat of higher costs is hanging over all of us.
Congress has the power to put a stop to this before even more people are priced out of their groceries. But we have to act NOW if we want to make sure Congress does its job.
[It only takes a minute: Will you sign our letter to Congress demanding that they take action against Trump’s tariffs?](https://click.everyaction.com/k/105668455/539001912/242149405?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNTkcvMS81NjE1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODgzNDNiNC0wODE3LWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Cc7bq04TV7EyXhQIL9RKY2UWfSjlkmZwwydKLt6mIzI=&emci=00f8f9fc-0117-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=088343b4-0817-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=6787172)

clean_body: I’m ready to change the tune in Washington, but I need you on my team. | Hey there, friend, It’s Marty O’Donnell—I’m the composer who scored the Halo video game franchise’s epic battles—now fighting a real one right here in Nevada’s 3rd Congressional District. I’ve got to tell you – the enthusiastic support I’ve received since relaunching my campaign in this critical battleground seat has me fired up! But my radical liberal opponent, Susie Lee , keeps making this easier. She just voted NO on the SAVE Act – a no-brainer bill that would require voter ID to stop non-citizens from voting and clean up our messy voter rolls. Apparently, Susie Lee wasn’t actually serious when she lectured us about defending our Democracy. Susie and the radical Left wanted us to show proof of COVID-19 vaccination just to enter buildings, but they couldn’t care less about proving you’re a citizen in order to cast a vote that determines the fate of our nation. Here’s the kicker: the Cook Political Report just flagged our district as a battleground seat that could decide who controls the House in 2026. They’re also giving Democrats a slight edge in the midterms, which means I’m ready to change the tune in Washington, but I need you on my team. She may have a long list that disqualifies her from being fit to cast a vote on our behalf in Congress, but that doesn’t mean she’s going to be easy to beat. Let’s show her that we aren’t just background noise—we’re the main track. Thanks, Marty O’Donnell Republican for Congress, NV-03 | ABOUT MARTY Marty O’Donnell isn’t a politician and he’s not taking any corporate PAC money. Marty will give us a voice – not special interests or Wall Street. It’s time to turn our nation around to make life better for Nevadans. Marty O’Donnell has an ear for solving problems. He’s an award-winning composer who wrote the iconic soundtracks for the video games Halo and Destiny. Marty will cut through the noise in DC. Marty O’Donnell will be a champion for Nevada families. So you wanna know a little more about what we’re fighting for...
#
Peter — here are five things we know to be true:
1. **Working people should be able to run for office.** Too often, the people we need running are discouraged simply because they don’t have the network or resources. We’re ready to flip the script.
2. **We need strong candidates up and down the ballot, in all 50 states.** In red states, purple states, and blue states — electing leaders at every level of government who will defend our freedoms is one big way we can take back our power.
3. **Corporate PACs and billionaire insiders have corrupted our politics.** Look no further than Elon Musk and his shady Super PAC, which has already spent hundreds of millions of dollars to influence our elections and our government.
4. **People-powered movements are one of the most effective tools to fight back.** That’s what we’re building together — a movement to take on the corporate elites, billionaires, and everyone else determined to strip away our rights.
5. **We need your support to continue this important work.** Whether it’s making a donation directly to Heartland Patriots or simply supporting the candidates we email you about, you are playing an instrumental role in our movement.

subject: Here's what you had to say:
body:
Sharing common themes from our NJ-09 priorities survey

| |
---
Team, Thank you to the hundreds of supporters who took the time to write in and share their thoughts with the campaign and with Nellie. Part of leadership is knowing when to listen, and that's exactly what we're doing. It's clear that countless folks from around NJ-09 and the country are fired up and ready to organize, speak out, and fight back against Donald Trump and Elon Musk. That's what we heard from many of you in our survey from the other day. Many of you stated your concern with executive overreach and Elon Musk's unchecked powers. We are too. We are fighting every day to hold this lawless and chaotic administration accountable. The economy and defending Social Security and Medicare were top concerns as well. At a time when the administration should be focused on bringing costs down, they're engaging in dangerous trade wars that will only increase costs for families. All while threatening to gut Medicaid and Social Security. The top concern was defending democracy. Nellie voted against the so-called SAVE Act because it will impose onerous restrictions on voting for millions of Americans — particularly women. It would also jeopardize the right to vote for every member of our military serving abroad. Nellie will always defend democracy and stand for safe and secure elections, the SAVE Act doesn't help with any of that. Thank you for writing in — we've forwarded your responses to Nellie as well because your opinion and ideas matter a great deal to her. [_**If you haven't yet taken our NJ-09 priorities survey, you can still do so here >>**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/105669634/539005587/-662131373?ms=250411_tp_survey_results&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTU0MDYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiM2Y2YjVjMDktMGQxNy1mMDExLThiM2QtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZmI3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=wVWAQA-OEu5ipzTzCOJVLhFP2MDSsQfRPE77yYBiwy8=&emci=a185071b-5316-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=3f6b5c09-0d17-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=17143604) Thank you for being part of our coalition. As we've been saying all along, the best way to counteract Trump is by regaining our House majority in 2026. Our race in NJ-09 is critical to that goal. — Nellie Pou HQ

### About Nellie Pou
Nellie Pou is the first Latina to represent New Jersey in Congress, and will be a target for the NRCC in 2026. As a mother and grandmother, Nellie knows what New Jersey families are facing and will continue to bring down costs while creating good-paying jobs. At a time when the administration should be focused on bringing costs down, they're engaging in dangerous trade wars that will only increase costs for families. It would also jeopardize the right to vote for every member of our military serving abroad. Nellie will always defend democracy and stand for safe and secure elections, the SAVE Act doesn't help with any of that. subject: AG Rayfield's First 100 Days in Office
body:
** First 100 Days in Office
------------------------------------------------------------

January 1, 2025 - April 10, 2025

In our first 100 days in office, we have shown our commitment to protecting Oregonians through proactive consumer protection initiatives, strategic legal challenges, and dedicated advocacy for vulnerable populations.

KEY ACCOMPLISHMENTS
Joined 13 Multi-State Lawsuits
Birthright Citizenship
DOGE One
DOGE Two
Fired Probationary Federal Workers
NIH Funding Cuts
Gender Affirming Care
Department of Education
Funding Freeze
HHS Funding Cuts
Elections Lawsuit Defending Oregon's Postmark Deadline for Ballots
NIH Grant Delays/Terminations Lawsuit
Gutting of Small Federal Agencies Lawsuit

Department of Education State Funding Lawsuit

Town Halls
2/20/25 - with Congresswoman Maxine Dexter

3/5//25 - with Arizona, Minnesota, and New Mexico AGs

3/10/25 - with Congresswoman Val Hoyle

3/17/25 - with Senators Wyden and Merkley & Congresswomen Bonamici, Dexter, Salinas, and Hoyle

3/26/25 - with Oregon state Senators Pham, Broadman, and Reynolds

4/3/25 - AARP tele town hall

4/9/25 - Eugene: Safeguarding Oregon Forum with Oregon House Speaker Julie Fahey

4/10/25 - Portland: Safeguarding Oregon Forum with Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes

** Legal Challenges
------------------------------------------------------------
* AG Dan Rayfield Challenges Unconstitutional Executive Order Ending Birthright Citizenship - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/attorney-general-dan-rayfield-challenges-unconstitutional-executive-order-ending-birthright-citizenship/)
* AG Rayfield Files Lawsuit with 22 States on Behalf of Oregonians to Block Trump Administration’s Freeze on Federal Grants - Oregon Department of Justice:https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/rayfield-files-lawsuit-with-22-states-on-behalf-of-oregonians-to-block-trump-administrations-freeze-on-federal-grants/Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/rayfield-files-lawsuit-with-22-states-on-behalf-of-oregonians-to-block-trump-administrations-freeze-on-federal-grants/)
* AG Rayfield Signs on to Multi-State Lawsuit involving Elon Musk and “DOGE” Access to the U.S. Department of Treasury - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/ag-rayfield-signs-on-to-multi-state-lawsuit-involving-elon-musk-and-doge-access-to-the-u-s-department-of-treasury/)
* AG Dan Rayfield Files Lawsuit to Block Order That Ends Funding for Medical Institutions, Gender-Affirming Care Research - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/ag-dan-rayfield-files-lawsuit-to-block-order-that-ends-funding-for-medical-institutions-gender-affirming-care-research/)
* AG Rayfield Sues Trump Administration For Defunding Medical And Public Health Innovation Research - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/ag-rayfield-sues-trump-administration-for-defunding-medical-and-public-health-innovation-research/)
* AG Rayfield Files Lawsuit to Stop Musk’s Power Grab - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/ag-rayfield-files-lawsuit-to-stop-musks-power-grab/)
* AG Rayfield Files Lawsuit to Stop Mass Firings of Federal Probationary - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/attorney-general-rayfield-files-lawsuit-to-stop-mass-firings-of-federal-probationary/)
* AG Rayfield Sues Trump Administration to Stop Dismantling of Department of Education and Protect Students - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (http://Attorney General Rayfield Sues Trump Administration to Stop Dismantling of Department of Education a)
* Elections EO (W.D. Wash.): OR/WA filed a lawsuit challenging the President’s election EO and defending our states’ postmark deadline for ballots: Media (https://oregoncapitalchronicle.com/2025/04/04/oregon-washington-sue-trump-over-sweeping-elections-order/)
* NIH grant delays/terminations (D. Mass.): Oregon and other states sued NIH for grant terminations, delays, and the “un-publishing” of notices of funding opportunities: Media (https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5232346-nih-grant-funding-states-lawsuit/)
* Gutting of small federal agencies (D.R.I.): Oregon and other states are challenging the EO gutting seven smaller federal agencies, including the Institute of Museum and Library Services: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/attorney-general-rayfield-sues-trump-administration-to-protect-libraries-and-museums/)
* Attorney General Rayfield Sues Trump Administration for Blocking Access to Hundreds of Millions of Dollars in Education Funds for State: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/attorney-general-rayfield-sues-trump-administration-for-blocking-access-to-hundreds-of-millions-of-dollars-in-education-funds-for-states/)

** Consumer Protection Initiatives
------------------------------------------------------------

* Secured 9.25-million-dollar settlement with two pharmaceutical giants for inflating prices.
* Submitted plan to end Google’s illigal monopoly over internet search engines.
* Joined a coalition in urging Congress to take action to address the rise in organized retail crime.
* Released 6-month report showing big results for Oregon Consumer Privacy Act (OCPA) in protecting consumer information online.
* Secured victory in battle against Ticketmaster/Live Nation over inflated ticket prices.

Attorney General Rayfield Issues Consumer Alert Regarding 23andMe Bankruptcy - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/attorney-general-rayfield-issues-consumer-alert-regarding-23andme-bankruptcy/)

Attorney General Rayfield Urges Consumers to Check Eligibility for Compensation for Inflated Generic Drug Prices - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/attorney-general-rayfield-urges-consumers-to-check-eligibility-for-compensation-for-inflated-generic-drug-prices/)

Attorney General Rayfield Releases 6 Month Report On Oregon Consumer Privacy Act - Oregon Department of Justice: Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/attorney-general-rayfield-releases-6-month-report-on-oregon-consumer-privacy-act/)

Attorney General Rayfield and Multi-State Coalition Submit Final Proposed Fix to End Google’s Search Monopoly - Oregon Department of Justice : Media (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/attorney-general-rayfield-and-multi-state-coalition-submit-final-proposed-fix-to-end-googles-search-monopoly/)

Consumer Complaints:
* 1,956 complaints closed (removing CAFAs, UTPA, APS, Elder Abuse, and any duplicated complaints)
* Total savings to consumers $311,245
* 307 complaints have reached a full or partial resolution

Online Toolkits:
* Updated online Consumer Privacy Toolkit (https://www.doj.state.or.us/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/DOJ-Privacy-Law-HowTo-Handout.pdf)
* Launched Gender Affirming Care Toolkit (https://www.doj.state.or.us/oregon-department-of-justice/civil-rights/gender-diverse-community-resources/)
* Updated Sanctuary State Toolkit (https://www.doj.state.or.us/oregon-department-of-justice/civil-rights/sanctuary-promise/community-toolkit/)
* Launched DEIA Toolkit for schools (https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/diversity-equity-inclusion-and-accessibility-deia-guidance-in-education/)
* Launched DEIA Toolkit for nonprofits (https://www.doj.state.or.us/oregon-department-of-justice/civil-rights/deia-guide-for-non-profits/)

** Settlements Secured for Oregon:
------------------------------------------------------------
Antitrust, False Claims, & Privacy Section - State of Oregon, v. Abbvie, Abbott Labs, Unimed Pharma, and Besins Healthcare

State antitrust lawsuit alleging Defendants filed sham patent litigation to delay market entry of generic competitors for its testosterone replacement drug, “AndroGel,” artificially raising prices paid in Oregon. We defeated Defendants’ motions to dismiss, and we reached a settlement for the payment of $9,250,000 including attorneys’ fee. The Court approved the settlement on March 13, 2025.

Civil Recovery Section – In 2025, the Civil Recovery Section has filed two actions seeking injunctive relief, ten actions to recover money owed to state agencies and ten petitions to appoint guardians for vulnerable Oregonians. It has also collected more than $100,000 in punitive damages that will be used to provide assistance to Oregon crime victims.

Upcoming Events:

Bend: Safeguarding Oregon Forum

Date: May 3, 2025

Time: 10 AM - 12:30 PM

Location: OSU-Cascades Campus, Edward J. Ray Hall - Atrium

Media Resources

High-resolution headshots available here (https://www.doj.state.or.us/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Rayfield-8x10-Headshot.pdf) .

One-on-one interviews with AG Rayfield can be requested by contacting Jenny Hansson at jenny.hansson@doj.oregon.gov (mailto:jenny.hansson@doj.oregon.gov)

[Your politics and policy brief for March 28, 2025](https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/f0257ea997931811)

Peter-

This week, Speaker Mike Johnson appointed me as the leader of a new effort in Congress to combat the Mexican drug cartels which has been my top priority in recent years. The House also cleared a key legislative hurdle to advance President Trump’s agenda and we advanced what is perhaps the most commonsense piece of legislation ever passed by the House of Representatives (which Democrats, of course, voted against).

My primary is less than a year away. If I win my primary, I will be re-elected to another term in the House of Representatives where I can continue fighting for you.

But this will not be an easy fight - there are already multiple candidates who have announced they are challenging me. They are backed by Trump-hating consultants and millions of dollars in anti-Trump money. We cannot let them flood this race with resources unopposed, which is why I need your help.

If you can spare any contribution at all, it will go a long way to help me win this race. You can donate here:

[CONTRIBUTE NOW >>](https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/f0257ea997931811)

A NEW EFFORT TO COMBAT THE CARTELS

[Chairman Crawford and Speaker Johnson Announce Creation of HPSCI Cartel Task Force]

[READ THE ANNOUNCEMENT HERE](https://intelligence.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=1520)

As you know, combating the Mexican drug cartels has been my top priority in Congress for the last several years. Now, there is a new effort in Congress that will give our efforts an extra boost under President Trump.

Speaker Mike Johnson and House Intelligence Committee Chairman Rick Crawford have created a new task force within the Intelligence Committee to combat the cartels, and appointed me as the leader of this effort.

The Cartel Task Force will support House Republicans’ efforts to build consensus with the U.S. Senate and the Trump Administration around identifying necessary legislative actions to combat the threat from the dangerous cartels in the Western Hemisphere involved in narcotics trafficking, human trafficking, the arms trade, and other illegal and destabilizing activities.

It is an honor to be entrusted by Speaker Johnson and Chairman Crawford with this position, and I remain as committed as ever to eliminating this grave threat to our country. With President Trump back in the White House, now is the time to act to ensure that the Administration has the tools and resources it needs to take the fight directly to the cartels that are ravaging our neighborhoods and killing American kids with fentanyl.

A BIG SET FORWARD IN ADVANCING THE TRUMP AGENDA

[Dan Crenshaw explains how House GOP can jam Senate GOP on reconciliation bill]

[WATCH MY TAKE ON THE CURRENT DEBATE OVER THE RECONCILIATION PACKAGE](https://x.com/lemm_power/status/1910391357916463309)

There was a major win in Congress this week for President Trump’s agenda.

The House cleared the way to extend President Trump’s tax cuts and prevent tax hikes. This vote kicks off reconciliation, which is critical to advancing the rest of President Trump’s agenda that he - and all Republicans - campaigned on.

There was an odd debate in the House of Representatives ahead of this vote. The usual suspects threatened to vote against it because it didn’t cut enough spending. To be clear: this doesn’t tie our hands to anemic budget cuts.

Republicans can still pursue $1.5 TRILLION in spending cuts—and that’s exactly what we’re going to do. The Senate set a baseline of $4 billion in cuts, which is why some members didn’t want to vote for it. But the baseline is exactly that - a baseline. The House will still lead the way and we will work to achieve the $1.5 trillion in savings that we promised voters.

THE MOST COMMONSENSE POLICY PASSES THE HOUSE

[Heres the Truth - SAVE Act doesnt stop women from voting]

[WATCH HERE](https://x.com/DanCrenshawTX/status/1910421034890670288)

Nearly 80% of Americans agree with voter ID and the basic notion that proof of citizenship should be required to vote in American elections. The House of Representatives followed the will of the American people this week, and passed commonsense legislation that would require states to verify that only American citizens are voting in their elections along with basic voter ID verification.

It is hard to imagine a more noncontroversial piece of legislation passing the House. This should have received unanimous, bipartisan support. But, of course, Democrats were against it. They even tried to push a lie that this bill somehow stopped women from voting and infringed on the voting rights of Americans.

It is an absurd lie, which I debunk in the video above. This is just another reminder that Democrats have learned nothing from the last election. Republicans will continue to stand for common sense. The left will continue to be against common sense. It’s just that simple.

SOCIAL MEDIA

[President Trump’s Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 brought taxes down and simplified filings for the vast majority of Americans. It was the most pro-growth, pro-family tax reform in modern history. This week, Congress will vote on the first step to preventing those tax cuts from expiring. I’m proud to stand with @POTUS to keep taxes low and wages up.](https://x.com/DanCrenshawTX/status/1909759156153991447)

[“Together, each for our own country, we will target and destroy those networks.” - Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at the Central American Security Conference in Panama. Bad time to be in the illicit fentanyl business.](https://x.com/DanCrenshawTX/status/1910056062503240133)

[The cartels turned a rehab center into a warzone. Mexico’s Secretariat of Security, @OHarfuch , says the “Los Chapitos” faction of the Sinaloa cartel stormed a facility in Culiacán — killed 9, injured 5, and abducted the owner, Guillermo Rodríguez Gaxiola. He was later found dead. The targets were rival Sinaloa members loyal to “El Mayo” — part of an ongoing power struggle between El Chapo’s sons and his longtime partner. These are the same cartel thugs flooding American cities with fentanyl — killing over 80,000 Americans a year.](https://x.com/DanCrenshawTX/status/1910081094914887896)

[Extraditions of narcos. Keep em coming. Great work by the Trump Administration and Mexico.](https://x.com/DanCrenshawTX/status/1910116350187422053)

NEWS

That's it for this week's campaign brief. Thank you for reading.

In service,

[Congressman and Former Navy SEAL](https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/end-of-quarter-deadline-cb)

Dan Crenshaw

name: David Hogg
subject: They called us turtles. We proved them wrong.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
We don’t need to be louder than the lies — we just need to be louder with the truth.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20250411-1&t=1&akid=1967%2E587540%2E4zqono)
Peter, when focus groups are asked what animal best represents the Democratic Party, do you know what they say? A turtle. Yes, a turtle. 🐢
Guess what animals they cite for Republicans? 🦁 Lions. 🦈 Sharks.
**That’s the perception — and it needs to change._Because here’s the reality:_**
Our generation is changing what it means to lead from the ground up. And we’re done with waiting for the same old politicians to make it happen.
Take Austin, Texas, where bold, progressive city council members spearheaded the **_largest_ zoning reform in any major U.S. city** — it was so effective that it lowered rents while prices skyrocketed elsewhere.
Or look at what we achieved after Uvalde — not just stronger background checks but the creation of the first-ever **Office of Gun Violence Prevention** at the White House. That office oversaw billions in funding and helped deliver the **_two largest_ one-year reductions in gun homicides in U.S. history.**

With all the challenges and uncertainty these days coming from the Trump administration and the failure of Congressional Republicans to do their jobs, I am doing allI can to organize, mobilize, and lead the fight to help Democrats take back the House in 2026.

I’ll be on the frontlines of sharing our message: lowering our costs, advancing our progress, and protecting our freedom. ## Ohio Woman Honors Forgotten Veterans
Christine Untrauer is [on a mission to honor veterans](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyckL9uwyAYxJ_G3oj482HHA0OXbOna0SLwgb8Wg4Wpo7x9lah9gY6nO53udx_X-WopUY7vdkUTYphbKHMoNZbWMB_YsNq8V7QpUcBZcqkZBybE7C2lx6x7bwKiRNWjESMAcKn00C9mOg9h4jetg3Newjj5AW5Wjtx7DMqKnsyzjYMQkgup9MlxEF4NAACTdEp1wNFTK_X0WSi3BUN6lAPryZW1T2Zpbds79dbJSycvG5Yt4dPq5KUsVNi9rDazVJxtlCP7zqutX-hZrPbAnf2xMcp7e-LlyF6JujP3q4UYBT_rqa_Gb3dKifZh7IDH1VJ6zWj_O-0w8icAAP__k-5-0Q) buried in unmarked graves across Portage County, Ohio. Drawing from her own family's military legacy, she's identified 49 veterans buried without markers at Maple Grove Cemetery, including four in a section for people who couldn't afford proper burials. Watch [a video report here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyc0LFuwyAQxvGnwVus4ziTZGCo1HpLpU4dLQKHTYVNRIgtv33lPkLX75N-w__7NtxsTHEZP-3MJoxhqCEPIZcx18rLypWLXZ6FbUox8ICA3QnoJOXgbUz70DXeBGZk1bCRZyICVJ1uJsMXxKtTDgFYagDNcLeXzrK-nzWTb6I5NCApESSqrnVA0itNRHRFp5QgYB9rLu1PjkudOKQ9r1xal-cmmanWx1OoN4G9wH7btnbPr_q68_Efi61uEqpfhXpPH6HfZ7lf5FdTjH9sMaX41GdBMM42pj-y_i_AavA3AAD__4ZYakI). While Veterans Affairs provides free markers, installation costs more--something Untrauer covers through donations. She aims to expand this work to all 29 cemeteries in the county, ensuring no veteran is forgotten.
## Locals Featured on Trading Cards in Japan
In the rural town of Kawara, Japan, children are swapping Pokemon for something a little more familiar: [handmade trading cards](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyckLGu4yAQAL8Gd1iwYDsuKK5xl2uvtPZgTTbBEGFkK39_uvf-4PWj0Wj-3Nc7cuIcf-NObovb2raybqXG0hrlkxpVzEclTIk3WkHBIJWVWq8BOX3WoQtuIwIyHTk9WWsVmGHsHm4O3t8mT-Ptb5j9MJGeAG9grIfZ-xE7dv9tymoNSoMZeq-sDma01toZvDHCKgrcSu2fhXN70JY-5aTa-7J3yT1aex_C_BKwCFiu6-pbeX3KRfSiHL4xAQvlRrUh551yE7DsHEIiiZGC3DHLVjFwjtJjDYeMRZ5cMUnO8olvzAKWrrrwvjglPsZJWBV35PQV0X627HTwLwAA__-_X35c) that feature local middle-aged men as their stars. The cards spotlight [real community members](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyckDuu2zAQRVdDdWPwKycFizTqXtqUwpgcSnzgR6AGFrz7wC9IFpBu5lzg4OL--lg_MJfctp9YyactrZz6mvrYOjO1JzENbOcgLCUnWrXUDqQFpdaIubxWN0WfiDSZiby6W2ulNm6edi_v-EATZQwJnZmdVMk9HomCC-4bIk7Zv23SKqWl0sbdgrQqmtlaa7_rYIywkmLmPm6fPTfeKZVXf9K4hV6n4nfm4xTmh9CL0Mt1XbcjbFj_5EIv7_sUegk4Ivx9WofOOw34R6EiM40TuEMlaP2CDL2VF1zY-E1DL4UCA-90EtQcYyHAjSJUbF-iE9LoFT7xwCb0Mg0fjyuXks_5LqzcKuby1Zr_b-On178DAAD__8Paj9Q) like retired fire chief Mr. Honda and soba noodle artisan Mr. Takeshita--each complete with stats, elemental powers, and lovingly drawn portraits. Sold exclusively at the Saidosho Center, these cards have quickly become cultural icons--turning everyday legends into collectible heroes.
## Trio of Strays Rescued Together, Stay Together
A real-life _Homeward Bound_ story unfolded in Vermont as two dogs and a cat--River, Rain, and Reed--were rescued after sticking together on the streets. See [their photo here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyckMFuGyEUAL-GvT0LHqwdHzi4rVY9NK2UROpxheHB0rAQAfZq-_WV-wm5j0aj-f08P5uYYg4_zUraBz93X2Zfaii9U75Tp2pyq2RSip5m5DgCVyDE7ExM-zwOTnsiJDmQFielFEc5HodFW3ry7kpHT1d3NiT4VeBVWsMFngWNdoj6YeNKCOQC5XiwXAknj0opdUYrJVOcXOylHv6UmPtCPu3lTvVgyzokvfT-0Zi8MJwYTtu2Hdot5729738fBMMplOIg09YYTuMJnxhOL2QS_Iie4HtZaTPVwZdyyw4QvpXQ4JIdXOCr6fBCzd7IwcV3qvDao32POcBbCdQXqvArw9tC8NorUW9D1e5jiynFdjwxxcNqYvof2j-39a7xXwAAAP__p5eJmA). After the rescue, it quickly became clear the animals had been through a lot. While the dogs warmed up quickly, the cat remained withdrawn--until he was reunited with his canine companions. The reunion was heart melting: head bonks, purrs, and cuddles revealed just how deep their bond ran. [Watch a report here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyc0LFuwyAQxvGnwVus4zjsemBoVWWolCpbRkTNYVMRkxJiK29fuY_Q9fuk3_C_nOzJxRSX6dNd2YQp2BqyDblMuVZeVq5c3HIv7FKKgS0C6gPQQUrrXUxPqxtvAjOyatjInogAle6a2RAMPYVBDgBBO88KETVRB1K7vnd9E82uAUmJIFHpdgSSXnVERAOOSgkC9rHm0n7nuNSZQ3rmlUs75muTzFzr7S7Uq8CjwOO2be0zP-rji_d_X1wdZ6GOq1Dv23j5SeeXt49zborxty2mFO9dLwimq4vpj6z_C7Aa_A0AAP__2aZplw). After their story was shared online, a compassionate couple offered to adopt all three and began a foster-to-adopt trial to ensure they could stay together for good.

name: Anderson Clayton (via Democrats.org)
subject: This case threatens not just one election, but the integrity of our entire democratic system
body:
I wanted to take a moment to explain what’s happening in North Carolina right now and what you can do to help:
---
Derek, I’m Anderson Clayton, the Chair of the North Carolina Democratic Party. I wanted to take a moment to explain what’s happening in North Carolina right now and what you can do to help: **In my state, there’s a case moving through the judicial system that threatens not just one election but the integrity of our entire democratic system.** Judge Jefferson Griffin lost his seat to North Carolina Justice Allison Riggs by 734 votes last November. And rather than concede, Griffin, backed by the Republican Party, has filed sweeping legal challenges attempting to discard tens of thousands of ballots. Last week, six months after Election Day, the Republican majority on the North Carolina Court of Appeals ruled that over _65,000_ voters whose ballots were already counted face having those ballots being thrown out unless they prove their eligibility. Ultimately, this decision will be appealed to our state’s Supreme Court. But here’s the thing: because we knew this would be a conflict of interest, Justice Allison Riggs has recused herself, making the makeup of the Supreme Court a 5-1 Republican advantage. We don’t know how these justices will rule, but we are prepared to continue this battle in federal court if it doesn’t go the way of democracy. This is the unprecedented fight that we are in right now, and it’s a test case for the right-wing playbook: If you can’t win the election, challenge the voters. Manufacture a list, create confusion, and let partisan courts do the rest. **We will not allow this to become the new normal in our state.** We will make sure we fight this on the ground, in the legislature, in the courts, and also at the ballot box next November. [**But this work is going to require a massive amount of resources, and we’re going to need all the help we can get. I wanted to take a moment to explain what’s happening in North Carolina right now and what you can do to help: In my state, there’s a case moving through the judicial system that threatens not just one election but the integrity of our entire democratic system. Judge Jefferson Griffin lost his seat to North Carolina Justice Allison Riggs by 734 votes last November. And rather than concede, Griffin, backed by the Republican Party, has filed sweeping legal challenges attempting to discard tens of thousands of ballots. Last week, six months after Election Day, the Republican majority on the North Carolina Court of Appeals ruled that over 65,000 voters whose ballots were already counted face having those ballots being thrown out unless they prove their eligibility. Ultimately, this decision will be appealed to our state’s Supreme Court. But here’s the thing: because we knew this would be a conflict of interest, Justice Allison Riggs has recused herself, making the makeup of the Supreme Court a 5-1 Republican advantage. We don’t know how these justices will rule, but we are prepared to continue this battle in federal court if it doesn’t go the way of democracy. This is the unprecedented fight that we are in right now, and it’s a test case for the right-wing playbook: If you can’t win the election, challenge the voters. Manufacture a list, create confusion, and let partisan courts do the rest. We will not allow this to become the new normal in our state. We will make sure we fight this on the ground, in the legislature, in the courts, and also at the ballot box next November.
